newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish ruling party support for EMU falls - poll.
newsitem.headline: Swedish ruling party support for EMU falls - poll.

text.p: Opposition towards Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) is growing within Sweden's ruling Social Democrat party, a poll in Swedish daily Svenska Dagbladet showed on Thursday.

Around 30 percent of the population say the country should say no to EMU compared to 27 percent polled in February while 35 percent say Sweden should wait a few years, the same number as at the time of the last poll.
The Swedish government is due to announce its decision soon on whether it will join EMU.
But the poll also signalled that uncertainty over EMU was fading slightly in some quarters, with 21 percent believing Sweden should join EMU from its 1999 start compared to 19 percent in February.
The survey of 1,100 people was conducted by pollster Skop from April 29 to May 22.

Within the ranks of the Social Democrats the desire to stand back and wait was stronger, with about 42 percent of the ruling party's supporters happy for the country to bide its time for a few years before joining -- down from 39 percent in February.
Only 13 percent say the country should join the first wave of the single currency in 1999 compared to 15 percent in February.
